episodes.213718: Monsoon moisture across eastern and southern New Mexico combined with daytime heating resulted in diurnal thunderstorm activity first across the higher terrain midday before moving into nearby lower elevations during the afternoon and evening hours on July 10th and 11th. Thunderstorms resulted in flash flooding and debris flow on and downstream of the burn scars surrounding Ruidoso both afternoons, and severe wind gusts near Ragland in Quay County the evening of July 10th and at two mesonet stations on White Sands Missile Range the evening of July 11th. Thunderstorms slowly diminished just before midnight both days.
episodes.213724: A lingering hot and humid airmass resulted in a few lines of thunderstorms as a front crossed the region. Moist atmospheric profiles inhibited more widespread or significant damaging wind gusts, though some storms did at least briefly become strong to severe.
episodes.213875: During the early morning hours of July 10th, storms brought damaging wind gusts to portions of western Missouri.
episodes.213888: A slow moving cold front stationed across northern Pennsylvania began to slowly sag southward during the daytime hours on July 10, 2026. This, coupled with sufficient instability and moisture over central Pennsylvania allowed for scattered instances of showers and thunderstorm to form across portions of central Pennsylvania. Storm motion parallel to the front allowed for training of thunderstorms, which allowed for isolated instances of flash flooding during the afternoon and evening hours in Centre, Cambria, and Blair Counties where soil was already saturated from recent heavy rainfall. Given the lack of bulk shear, thunderstorms largely stayed sub-severe outside of a thunderstorm in northern Northumberland County that became marginally severe with numerous reports of tree damage in and around Turbotsville.
episodes.213927: Thunderstorms moved across western North Carolina then raced eastward into a very hot and deeply mixed airmass across the eastern Carolinas.  Thunderstorm cells grew into rapidly eastward-moving line segments which produced widespread wind damage.  As the storms crossed into slightly cooler marine air streaming onshore they weakened rapidly as they approached the coast.
episodes.213928: Thunderstorms moved across western North Carolina then raced eastward into a very hot and deeply mixed airmass across the eastern Carolinas.  Thunderstorm cells grew into rapidly eastward-moving line segments which produced widespread wind damage.  As the storms crossed into slightly cooler marine air streaming onshore they weakened rapidly as they approached the coast.
episodes.214195: Showers and thunderstorms developed in a hot and humid airmass. Some storms produced damaging winds and locally heavy rainfall.
episodes.214207: A focused shortwave pushed eastward out of the Appalachians during the early afternoon hours of July 10th. This interacted with an unstable atmosphere, with atmospheric profiles favorable for damaging winds. Multiple strong downbursts occurred, with several instances of significant wind damage especially in Augusta and Whitmire.
episodes.214208: A focused shortwave pushed eastward out of the Appalachians during the early afternoon hours of July 10th. This interacted with an unstable atmosphere, with atmospheric profiles favorable for damaging winds. Multiple strong downbursts occurred, with several instances of significant wind damage especially in Augusta and Whitmire.
episodes.214213: Numerous thunderstorms developed through the evening hours due to an advancing cold front and very unstable atmosphere. Some of these storms became severe and produced instances of damaging winds.
episodes.214554: A thunderstorm moving through brought a wind gust to 73 mph at the Denver International Airport.
episodes.214581: For the second time this summer, heavy rain from thunderstorms across the upper Big Sioux River Basin brought rises to the Big Sioux River itself. The river gauges at both Estelline and Bruce both briefly rose into Minor Flood Stage before quickly falling by mid month.
episodes.214756: A broad area of high pressure shifted sufficiently to allow moisture to creep into Utah, and in combination with strong daytime heating, resulted in daily convection with instances of severe and damaging wind gusts, as well as some flooding.
episodes.214798: Thunderstorms moved across portions of northern Illinois.
episodes.214845: Typical summer weather prevailed with scattered afternoon and evening storms, some of which were severe. Unfortunately, two fatalities occurred in Tallahassee on July 10th when a large tree fell on a moving vehicle.
episodes.214945: Typical summer weather prevailed with scattered afternoon and evening storms, some of which were severe.
episodes.214947: Typical summer weather prevailed with scattered afternoon and evening storms, some of which were severe.
episodes.215038: Thunderstorms produced heavy rainfall, flash flooding, and isolated wind damaging across northern Ohio.
episodes.215271: Despite drier air aloft affecting portions of the area thanks to the Saharan Air Layer, enough moisture and instability was in place for scattered to numerous showers and thunderstorms to develop across northeast FL. Southwest flow mainly focus isolated strong to severe convection over the eastern half of the region. Presence of dry air aloft likely played into stronger downbursts and areas of wind damage across northeast FL.
episodes.215284: A subtle shortwave moving over Wyoming combined with ample monsoon moisture lead to strong thunderstorms and heavy rain in Nebraska.
episodes.215358: A thunderstorm produced large hail in Osage County on the evening of July 9.
episodes.215359: A series of thunderstorms tracked across the Missouri Ozarks during the overnight hours of July 9 into July 10. These storms produced very heavy rainfall. A swath of 7 to 12 inches of rain was recorded in about 7 hours leading to widespread flash flooding especially near mountain creeks and streams. The flooding peaked in the early morning hours of July 10, but rescue operations for victims stranded by flooding continued well into the day.
episodes.215429: Scattered thunderstorms developed across portions of southeast Georgia in the early evening hours along a surface trough. A few of these storms became strong enough to produce damaging wind gusts.
episodes.215430: Scattered thunderstorms developed just inland of the coast in the early evening hours. These thunderstorms then steadily tracked to the coast and produced strong wind gusts at several observation sites.
episodes.215456: Clusters of thunderstorms developed along the sea breeze in the afternoon hours along the southeast South Carolina coast. A few of these storms became strong enough to produce damaging wind gusts and hail into the early evening hours.
episodes.215462: A persistent cluster of thunderstorms developed in the early afternoon hours and produced areas of very heavy rainfall in and around the Charleston metro area. Several instances of flash flooding occurred, mainly in the form of flooded and impassable roadways. Rainfall amounts for the event generally ranged from 2 to 4 inches, with a few isolated amounts in excess of 4 inches.
episodes.215463: Clusters of thunderstorms developed inland near the southeast South Carolina coast in the afternoon and early evening hours. These storms eventually moved into the Atlantic coastal waters through the late evening and produced strong wind gusts.
episodes.215528: An isolated severe thunderstorm downed a tree in Cass County Indiana on the evening of July 10.
episodes.215626: A trough centered over the Great Lakes provided the impetus for showers and thunderstorms. One storm complex, consisting of a bow echo, moved across the southernmost counties of East Tennessee, producing thunderstorm wind damage in Bradley County.
episodes.215748: Severe thunderstorms briefly impacted south-central Kansas during the evening hours of July 9th. Damaging wind gusts near 60 mph and hail up to golf ball size were reported.
episodes.215764: A mesoscale convective system tracked from north of St. Louis to near Terre Haute during the late afternoon and early evening, triggering scattered severe thunderstorms.  A wet microburst downed a few trees on the north side of Effingham while a second storm knocked down a tree limb in Lawrenceville.  Pockets of heavy rain occurred with an observer in Casey in Clark County measuring 3.50.
episodes.215765: An upper level low triggered scattered afternoon and evening thunderstorms.  Numerous funnel clouds were reported near the I-74 corridor, with one tornado briefly touching down in a field in rural eastern McLean County.  A wet microburst flattened crops northeast of Pana late in the evening.
episodes.216158: Strong afternoon heating within a weakly sheared, moist environment leads to a strongly unstable environment coupled with steep low level lapse rates supportive of a cluster of strong to severe thunderstorms that produces multiple severe wind gusts while moving northwestward across southwest and west central Florida, and severe hail in west central Florida.
episodes.216159: Strong afternoon heating within a weakly sheared, moist environment leads to a strongly unstable environment coupled with steep low level lapse rates supportive of a cluster of strong to severe thunderstorms that produces numerous strong and several severe marine wind gusts as it overspreads adjacent coastal waters while moving northwestward across southwest and west central Florida.
episodes.216179: An area of low pressure across Kentucky and the southern Appalachians led to the development of a line of showers and thunderstorms across western Virginia and western North Carolina during the afternoon hours. This line of storms intensified as it tracked into the Piedmont and Coastal Plain of central North Carolina in the late afternoon and early evening. Widespread damaging wind reports were observed.
episodes.216192: Over the course of several days between July 6th and July 9th, an unsettled pattern persisted across the Ohio and Tennessee Valley as a cutoff low meandered across the region. A humid, unstable environment was present throughout this time period with dew point temperatures in the mid 70s and precipitable water values near or exceeding 2 inches. On top of this, relatively weak steering flow in the mid-levels of the atmosphere lead to slow movement of showers and thunderstorms which developed, resulting in localized heavy rainfall amounts and flash flooding. Scattered flash flooding occurred across central Kentucky over the four day period, with severe weather impacts mainly being limited to isolated downbursts from hydrometeor loading in otherwise disorganized cells. However, by the 9th, the ingestion of the cutoff low into broader troughing did provide for slightly stronger wind shear and better storm organization. With a seasonably humid and unstable environment remaining in place, this stronger wind shear did promote a bit more coverage of strong to severe storms, with a couple wind damage reports and a spin-up tornado being observed during the evening and early nighttime hours on July 9th.
episodes.216197: Multiple rounds of severe thunderstorms moved through Missouri on July 9 and into the morning of July 10. The first round of severe thunderstorms came through portions of west central and central Missouri during the morning of July 9. This cluster of thunderstorms produced damaging wind gusts of 60 to 70 mph winds, resulting in damage to numerous trees. A second round produced severe thunderstorms over central into south central Missouri on the evening and night of July 9 into the morning of July 10. This resulted in a brief tornado in Rolla, in addition to a few instances of flash flooding. Localized rainfall amounts of 3 to 6 inches were observed from Maries through Dent counties.
episodes.216265: An isolated stronger storm produced high winds that stripped the leaves off the corn and beans 5 miles south of Revillo.
episodes.216285: A complicated environment was in place across the area as a storm system moved across the area with numerous outflow boundaries across the area. These allowed scattered showers and storms to develop across the area. An isolated severe storm during the afternoon and produced a downburst that damaged a shed and knocked down a tree. Storms interacting with outflow boundaries causing several funnel clouds to develop.
episodes.216287: Numerous outflow boundaries sat across eastern Iowa on the 9th as a weak storm system  moved across the area. Scattered showers and storms developed across the area and interacted with these outflow boundaries causing funnel clouds to develop during the afternoon and early evening hours.
episodes.216289: A complicated environment was in place across the area as a storm system moved across the area with numerous outflow boundaries in placed.  Storms interacting with outflow boundaries causing several funnel clouds to develop. A landspout was reported in Henry County that was rated EFU because there was no visible damage.
episodes.216333: An upper high was located near the southern Arizona/California border with north to northeast flow across the region.  Storms developed off of the higher terrain and pushed onto the lowlands, bringing wind gusts over 70 mph and some blowing dust to the Lordsburg Playa.
episodes.216337: A shortwave trough tracked through southern Canada and pushed a cold front through the state, leading to scattered thunderstorms across central North Dakota through the afternoon and evening. There were numerous reports of severe hail across central North Dakota, as well as damaging wind gusts, with the most damage across Wells and Stutsman County. The largest hail reported was 2.5 inches in diameter near Silva in Pierce County and near Heimdal in Wells County. The strongest estimated wind gust was 80 mph north of Streeter in Stutsman County, where there was notable tree damage, a couple of grain bins blown away, and a pole barn that lost its roof.
episodes.216491: Another day with moisture streaming over a high pressure brough more thunderstorms the region. Storms developed off the higher terrain and pushed east, growing upscale into a large line of storms as the pushed towards the Colorado and Kansas border. While doing so, they produced strong winds.
episodes.216492: Another day with moisture streaming around a high pressure system to southwest would bring additional thunderstorms to the eastern plains. Some of the stronger cluster of storms would go on to produce severe wind gusts.
episodes.216611: During the evening hours of July 9th, a few clusters of thunderstorms merged into a broken squall line and moved east across portions of east-central and northeast Colorado. Wind gusts up to 69 mph were measured in Yuma County. No damage was reported.  Zero visibility was reported near Eckley from blowing dust associated with the thunderstorm winds.
episodes.216641: During the evening hours on the 9th, severe weather impacted portions of southwest Nebraska. Initially, a splitting supercell produced golfball sized hail in Dundy County. A few hours later after these supercells diminished, a squall line approaching from the west produced a 64 mph gust in Dundy County.
episodes.216716: An upper level disturbance, moving through weak northwest flow aloft, interacted with an unstable airmass featuring MLCAPEs around 3000 J/kg across the Mid-South by the afternoon of July 9, 2026. As a result, a complex of thunderstorms developed over southeast Missouri and moved into northeast Arkansas and the Missouri Bootheel. The instability combined with 15 to 30 knots of shear supported a few severe storms with damaging winds.
episodes.216757: A moist, weakly forced summertime pattern persisted across the northern Gulf Coast on July 10th. Southerly onshore flow maintained abundant low-level moisture while scattered marine convection was favored during the morning hours. A waterspout developed beneath a thunderstorm approximately southeast of Gulfport and was observed on a traffic camera.
episodes.216830: During the mid to late evening hours on the 9th, an intense broken line of thunderstorms raced east across portions of northwest and west-central Kansas. Numerous reports of damaging straight-line winds were reported, including an 81 mph measured gust in Sherman County. Additionally, a few supercells moving slowly southeast ahead of the line of storms produced one inch hail in both Cheyenne and Rawlins Counties.
episodes.216839: Throughout much of the afternoon and evening on July 8th, severe storms moved slowly through northeast Iowa with several inches of rain in some locations. This resulted in isolated flash flooding along with rises into flood stage along portions of the Cedar and Upper Iowa River basins. Additionally, these storms produced severe wind gusts which resulted in scattered instances of tree damage.
episodes.216997: Scattered strong storms with gusty winds resulted in strong winds across portions of the Chesapeake Bay, James River, and Atlantic coastal waters.

episodes.217039: Strong heating and high humidity resulted in isolated storms with gusty winds.

Multiple severe thunderstorms occurred, producing mainly small swaths of damaging wind gusts. An EF1 tornado was also reported across Cleveland and Lincoln Counties.
episodes.217143: Scattered thunderstorms and storm clusters moved into upstate South Carolina from North Carolina during the afternoon. Several of the storms produced mostly small swaths of damaging wind gusts.
episodes.217146: Scattered thunderstorms and storm clusters moved into northeast Georgia from North Carolina during the afternoon. A couple of the storms produced small swaths of damaging wind gusts over the Piedmont.
episodes.217160: A slow moving front produced scattered thunderstorms across southeastern PA and NJ.

episodes.217170: Scattered thunderstorms initiated off of a stalled boundary along the Interstate 80 corridor. While predominantly a flooding day with taller and skinnier CAPE, low DCAPE values, and weak shear, one storm in northwestern Pennsylvania became strong enough to produce wind damage. Training thunderstorms along the stalled boundary lead to flash flooding in eastern Ohio, northern West Virginia and western Pennsylvania in the afternoon and evening on July 10th. episodes.217182: Isolated gale-force wind gusts occurred in association with a thunderstorm moving quickly northwest from the Straits of Florida to the southwest of Key West.  A weak lower tropospheric trough was moving westward through the Keys with an upper level low centered over the central Bahamas.
episodes.217183: An inverted lower tropospheric trough associated with an upper trough of low pressure moved west through the Florida Keys and adjacent coastal waters during the afternoon and evening hours of July 10, 2026.  Numerous showers and thunderstorms developed over the Straits of Florida and Cuba, with resultant outflow boundaries focusing new development of showers and thunderstorms inside the reef tract and across the Florida Keys.  Numerous gale-force wind gusts were measured in association with the stronger thunderstorms and outflow boundaries.
episodes.217262: An upper level disturbance arrived and lingered over South Florida in early to mid June which produced a period of unsettled weather.
episodes.217289: Continuing an active monsoon period with multiple recorded wind gusts of 60 to 64 mph in Graham, Cochise and Santa Cruz counties. The severe thunderstorm winds caused damage to a house's porch and greenhouse in Sierra Vista. Additionally, the strong outflow winds from thunderstorms caused a dust storm in Cochise County that reduced visibilities to below 1/4 miles.
episodes.217437: A diffuse surface frontal boundary became the focus for scattered thunderstorm development early in the evening of July 9th. Most of these storms were sub-severe, however a few of the stronger storms did produce some marginally severe hail and an isolated thunderstorm wind damage report.
episodes.217439: A second round of severe weather moved across portions of the NWS Dodge City area of responsibility late in the evening into the overnight on July 9th (into calendar day July 10th). A tornado developed and hit a home in the 7700 block of Brownsville Road, lifting up both the front porch and the carport roof that were attached to the house. The pillars under the front porch shifted slightly, but the pillars under the carport fell over, allowing the roof to land on two cars parked there. The resident was sitting on his front porch just before the tornado hit and noticed it got hotter and more humid ahead of the rain and wind. He was just able to get inside before it hit.||The tornado then skipped over mostly open fields before hitting a couple of trees, knocking down branches, and then a barn in the 9600 block. The sides of this barn were well anchored to the ground, but the roof was able to peel off. Portions of this roof |were strewn east southeast up to 0.4 miles downstream. Residents in this area noted how calm conditions were just before the tornado hit and then it got calm again. ||The tornado then turned southeastward where it heavily damaged a barn and snapped a large cedar tree at the intersection of Jetson Road and Brownsville Road. No other damage was noted downstream of this location.

A NWS ground survey determined an EF0 tornado was on the ground for 0.72 miles, with peak winds of 80 to 85 mph and a 200 yard wide path. The tornado touched down along the Homelife Plaza and traveled south before lifting near Soest Road in Rolla. The tornado caused damage to trees and roofs of several businesses along the path, with debris laying in convergent patterns along the path.

Rain began at about 10PM on the 9th, but heavy rain continued through most of the night. Flash flooding began along the East and Middle Forks of the Black River at around midnight, but the rain kept coming. By morning a swath of 10 to 12 inches of rain had fallen across northeast Reynolds County, with most of that water flowing quickly through the Black River basin. Nearly the entire flood plain was inundated including many camp sites near the rivers. The Lesterville area was particularly hard hit. Hundreds of people were stranded by flood waters including more than 200 children and staff at Camp Taum Sauk on the Black River. The USGS river gage on the Black River near Annapolis recorded an all time record crest of 28.7 feet.

The rain began around 10pm but continued through the night. A swath of 10 to 12 inches of rain fell from near Viburnum to Taum Sauk Mountain to east of Annapolis. A report of 12.25 inches was measured 6 miles northeast of Oates. Flash flooding began around midnight and peaked just before dawn. All creeks and rivers in the area overflowed their banks with water inundating numerous camp sites as well as some homes and roadways. Several residents were forced to evacuate.
A 58 mph wind gust was measured by a personal weather station.
A 70 mph thunderstorm wind gust was measured by the Hays Regional Airport AWOS.
The thunderstorm wind gust was recorded by an Ambient Weather Network station.

Rain began at about 10PM on the 9th, but heavy rain continued through most of the night. Flash flooding began shortly after midnight, peaking just before dawn. By morning, a swath of 5 to 7 inches of rain had fallen across the southern portion of the county from Courtois to Belgrade. Most creeks and rivers in this area overflowed their banks. Water was reported over the road in numerous locations along Highway C.

Rain began around 10PM on the evening of July 9, but storms increased in intensity and persistence shortly after midnight. By morning, a swath of 7 to 10 inches of rain had fallen across southern Crawford County from near Cedar Ford to near Viburnum. This led to flash flooding along every creek and river in the area, with much of this water flowing through the Huzzah Creek. Camp sites along the river were inundated as well as homes and roadways. Numerous water rescues and evacuations were required. One person was killed in floodwaters after her home was swept off its foundation with her inside.

Heavy rainfall across portions of southeast Minnesota and northeast Iowa resulted in increased runoff into the Upper Iowa River Basin. Consequently, downstream flow resulted in the Upper Iowa River at Bluffton to rise into flood stage during the morning on July 10th. The river crested in minor flood stage at 12.55 feet before falling below flood stage during the evening on July 10th.

The tornado continued east into the northwest corner of Lincoln County near the intersection of Old State Highway 18 and Highway 18.
